ConocoPhillips gained 0.64% today as oil prices steadied, but the stock has declined 3.5% over two weeks as crude has weakened—US oil fell from above $134 to $83.90 per barrel. The sharp drop reflects the market's growing skepticism about the severity of Middle East supply disruptions. A U.S. Navy blockade is cutting Iranian exports, but six months into the conflict, markets are treating the stalemate as a permanent fixture rather than an acute crisis, which removes the price-support premium crude enjoyed earlier.

For refiners and integrated producers like ConocoPhillips, cheaper oil is a mixed blessing. Lower crude costs help profitability if margins hold, but the collapse in prices over two weeks signals that investors no longer expect sustained supply tightness from the Iran conflict—the opposite of what energy stocks bet on when geopolitical tension first spiked.
